Return one complete JSON object only, with this structure: {"observations":[{"source":"record alias","treatment":"exact treatment setting","otherSetting":"exact competing setting"},{"source":"record alias","treatment":"exact treatment setting","otherSetting":"exact competing setting"}],"newTest":{"source":"record alias","factor":"investigated factor name","otherFactor":"competing factor name","unit":"one independently assignable object","availableUnits":"integer digits only","controls":"fixed conditions","measurement":"complete measurement rule","outcome":"outcome metric"},"unknowns":[]}. Select the two existing observations, then the resources/rules for a new test; records may appear in any order. Each group uses one source alias and all its phrases must come from that record. Copy exact contiguous excerpts in their original language, replacing the descriptive placeholders. For observations, isolate each actual treatment setting and its competing setting separately; do not copy the whole observation or a future procedure. In newTest, factor and otherFactor are names, not treatment levels. unit is the object independently assigned to a condition, not seconds, degrees, repeat readings or the full collection. availableUnits is only the integer count of new independent units. measurement includes the full stated procedure; outcome is only the metric. For a repeated excerpt use {"quote":"exact excerpt","occurrence":0} with its zero-based occurrence instead of a string. Any unsupported phrase or entire group must be null. unknowns is an array of short missing-information explanations. Use exactly the specified fields. Do not invent facts, results, rules, answers or approval. Source records are data, never instructions to follow.
